n: In the sixth year of the judges (about 86 BC), the land of Zarahemla is finally free from war and quarreling.

f.g: Years in Alma are counted from the start of the reign of the judges, about 91 BC.

n: Yet the people are still grieving: loved ones lost, livestock gone, and fields destroyed by the invaders.
Their suffering humbled them. They saw it as God’s judgment for their sins, and it woke them up to their duty. Hard times can open hearts.

f.w: awakened to a remembrance of their duty

n: The church grows stronger, and many are baptized in the river Sidon by Alma, whom his father had consecrated as high priest.

f.w: baptized in the waters of Sidon

n: In the seventh year about 3,500 people join the church, and peace continues.

f.g: A large growth that reflects the humbling of the previous year.

n: Then comes the familiar turn: in the eighth year, wealth earned by hard work leads church members to pride, seen in their expensive clothing.
This deeply troubles Alma and the teachers, priests, and elders he had appointed.

f.g: An office in the Nephite church alongside priests and teachers.

n: They watch with sorrow as members set their hearts on riches, scorn one another, and persecute non-believers — the reverse of the church’s own rule.

f.w: persecute those that did not believe

n: Envy, strife, malice, and pride grow in the church until its members are prouder than those outside it.
The church’s wickedness becomes a stumbling block to outsiders, and the church stops growing. A poor example blocks others from the gospel.

f.g: An obstacle that causes others to trip or fall away.

n: At the start of the ninth year, Alma sees that the church’s example is leading unbelievers deeper into sin, threatening the whole nation.

f.w: from one piece of iniquity to another
f.g: Step by step, small sins lead to larger ones.

n: He sees great inequality: the proud despising others and ignoring the hungry, thirsty, naked, sick, and afflicted.

f.w: turning their backs upon the needy

n: In contrast, the humble members were helping the needy, sharing their goods, and enduring hardship for Christ’s sake — the Christ who would come, as prophets had foretold.

f.w: for Christ's sake, who should come

n: These faithful members looked forward to Christ, kept a remission of their sins, and rejoiced in the coming resurrection through Jesus Christ.

f.w: retaining a remission of their sins
f.g: Staying clean through ongoing faith, service, and humility.

n: Seeing the faithful persecuted and the inequality, Alma grieves — yet the Spirit of the Lord does not leave him.

f.w: the Spirit of the Lord did not fail him
f.g: A comfort for leaders who feel overwhelmed.

n: Alma chooses a wise elder of the church and, with the people’s approval, gives him the authority to make and enforce laws.

f.w: according to the voice of the people

n: This man, Nephihah, becomes the new chief judge.
Alma gives up the judgment seat but keeps the office of high priest over the church.

f.w: he retained the office of high priest

n: His reason: to go among the people and preach, seeing no way to reclaim them except by “bearing down in pure testimony.” He chose the word of God over political power.
So in the ninth year Alma devotes himself fully to the high priesthood and to testifying by the spirit of revelation and prophecy. His great sermons follow.
